title: Go Beyond Black-box Policies: Rethinking the Design of Learning Agent for Interpretable and Verifiable HVAC Control
problem: Existing MBRL methods for HVAC systems rely on black-box thermal dynamics models and stochastic optimizers, lacking reliability guarantees and risking occupant safety. Current approaches cannot provide verifiable or interpretable control policies.
motivation: Energy-efficient HVAC control is critical for sustainability and occupant safety, requiring interpretable and provably reliable decision-making algorithms.
method: Decision tree policies are extracted from thermal dynamics models using importance sampling to reduce high dimensionality. A novel verification criterion based on domain knowledge is introduced, combined with an offline verification algorithm that guarantees control policy reliability.
key_novelty: Using decision tree extraction with domain-knowledge-based verification to create interpretable and provably reliable HVAC control policies from black-box thermal models.
contributions: Novel verification criterion for RL agents in HVAC control based on domain knowledge
Policy extraction procedure producing verifiable decision tree policies with importance sampling for dimensionality reduction
Offline verification algorithm that guarantees control policy reliability
68.4% more energy savings and 14.8% comfort improvement with 1127× computation overhead reduction versus SOTA
limitations: Generalization to other control domains and scalability challenges not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Interpretable and verifiable HVAC control via decision trees
